articleTitle: An Autonomous Mobile Robot Platform for Medical Purpose
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Engineering and Application (ICSEEA)

authors.preferredName: Catur Hilman A. H. B. Baskoro

abstract: An autonomous mobile robot is a mobile robot that can execute a path-plan autonomously to perform certain behaviors or tasks. This paper presents the hardware overview consist of mechanical design, motion control system, and modular subsystem of ROM20. ROM20 is an autonomous mobile robot platform that is being developed at the Research Center for Electrical Power and Mechatronics, Indonesian Institute of Sciences (RCEPM-LIPI) for medical purpose. ROM20 uses four stepper motors connected to four mecanum wheels. The motion control system is based on UART serial communication on each pin TX and RX of two microcontroller and bluetooth module. On top of the ROM20 is the modular which can be replaced with several subsystems such as Ultraviolet type C (UVC) lamp irradiation, disinfectant mist sprayer, and food delivery warmer. ROM20 can be controlled via bluetooth communication with a distance up to 22 meters. The space used by ROM20 for maneuver in any directions is around 63 cm × 63 cm of square tile.

articleTitle: Performance Comparison of Proportional-Integral and Fuzzy-PI for a Droop Control of DC Microgrid
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Engineering and Application (ICSEEA)
abstract: This work presents the droop control performance for sharing loads on the DC microgrid network. The traditional droop control consists of voltage control and current control where the PI controller is used as compensation for the error. The droop control performance can be seen from the fast response of the system when load power sharing between two DC generating sources is enabled. The Fuzzy-PI controller as an intelligent control functions to improve the performance of droop control on the DC microgrid. The Fuzzy PI controller suggested is built with the aid of a closed loop control based on the power of each unit DCG (DC Generator), and accurate power distribution has been realized proportionally to the power ratings of each DCG taking into account load changes. The use of Fuzzy-PI in droop control makes the dynamic reaction quicker (0. 06s rise time) and microgrid system stability better compared with PI controllers. The proposed control strategy is completely tested with a Mathlab/Simulink simulation.

articleTitle: Comparison Model of Buck-boost and Zeta Converter Circuit using MPPT Control Incremental Conductance Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Engineering and Application (ICSEEA)
abstract: Solar energy is currently being developed, one of the technologies being photovoltaic (PV) panels. The PV can generate electrical energy by absorbing sunlight through an extraordinary process. Due to the increased demand for electrical energy, the DC-DC converter is one component of the PV system that is installed to meet these energy needs. The Maximum Power Point Tracker (MPPT) control system is then mounted to monitor the maximum power point close to the characteristics of the PV frame. This paper addressed the subject matter of the MPPT Incremental Conductance (IC) Algorithm using a comparative study of the effects of the Buck-boost and Zeta Converter Circuit Modeling. Both DC-DC converters are designed for a 1 kWp PV network that has been proposed to use a grid-connected PV network with an output voltage above 360 V. Simulations are conducted under Standard Test Condition with various irradiance conditions ranging from 100 to 1000 W/m2 and 25°C temperatures. The result of the modeling shows that the output of the solar panels is consistent with the power characteristics of the changes in irradiance and temperature. The zeta converter has the best performance with 94 % efficiency and high response time compared to the buck-boost converter with only 90% efficiency. Nonetheless, all circuits with MPPT control IC algorithms are still used to maintain output at full efficiency.

articleTitle: Implementation of Photovoltaic Water Spray Cooling System and Its Feasibility Analysis
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Engineering and Application (ICSEEA)
abstract: This paper discusses the effects of applying a cooling system on photovoltaic (PV) designed using water sprays controller to improve efficiency and increasing power output. The cooling system was attached on existing 400 W polycrystalline PV panels. The PV temperature is maintained by controller at 30° C against rising temperatures above it by spraying water using 32 nozzles on the back side of the panel surface. PV testing with cooling system was carried out by including non-cooled PV panels for comparison. Then effect of temperature on the PV output power including the cooling system losses analyzed, net power and increasing in efficiency presented. Finally, the overall use of a water spray cooling system on PV panels was evaluated. Test results showed the PV output power with the cooling system increased by 9.03% compared to the non-cooled PV. The increase in temperature per degree above 30 °C caused PV output power decreases 0.411%. Overall, by involving the calculation of system losses the net PV output power gain becomes 4.09%.

articleTitle: Study on Combustion of Range Extender Spark Ignition Engine Fueled with Biogas
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Engineering and Application (ICSEEA)
abstract: A study on combustion of range extender spark ignition engine fueled with biogas was conducted using a simulation method in BOOST AVL software. The study was conducted using a two cylinders range extender based spark ignition engine for 35 kW of an electric vehicle fueled with gasoline-biogas mixed varied from 0 to 100% by volume. The biogas fuel in this study is represented as high purity biogas after purifying process which mainly contains CH4 or methane. The engine was operate on 3500 rpm and biogas was fumigated into the intake manifold. The results showed that the highest in-cylinder pressure obtained from engine fueled with 80% biogas. Meanwhile, the lowest in-cylinder temperature resulted from the engine fueled with 100% of biogas. Finally, the emission of CO and HC increase with the increases of biogas content, while the NOx is decrease when the biogas content increases.

articleTitle: Optimal PV Farm Size and Location Determination in Kudus Distribution System Using Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO)
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Engineering and Application (ICSEEA)
abstract: Along with the rising demand for electrical energy, and also considering government policies to increase renewable energy mix in the primary energy sources, a new renewable energy generating unit is needed. PV farm integration as distributed generation (DG) can be used as the solution to both problems. PV installations are considered a suitable solution since it used renewable energy. However, misplacement or unsuitable capacity of PV installations in the distribution systems can possibly worsen the system quality, thus optimization is needed to ensure that the goal is achieved by also improve the system quality. This paper presents the optimization of the location and sizing of PV farm using Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) in order to reduce losses and voltage drop as well as increasing the overall system reliability. The results indicate that the PV installations with the optimized locations and sizes can reduce the losses and voltage drop and increase the system reliability.

articleTitle: Population Balance and Computational Fluid Dynamics Modeling of Swirl Flow Microbubble Generator
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Engineering and Application (ICSEEA)
abstract: Microbubbles technology has become an issue that has attracted the attention of researchers in the last decade, because it has a wide application in various fields, one of which is for water treatment. However, the design of microbubble generators involving multi-phase studies remains a challenge in producing efficient designs. In this study, the design involved multi-phase modeling based on the Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) coupled with the Population Balance Method (PBM) was used to predict the size distribution of microbubbles. Two coalescence models (Luo model and Turbulent model) and two breakage models (Luo model and Lehr model) were investigated to determine their compatibility with test results using Particle Image Velocimetry (PIV). Based on the CFD-PBM simulation, the bubble size distribution was predicted successfully. The combination of the Turbulent coalescence model and the Lehr breakage model has the best compatibility with experimental results (PIV) so that it can be used as a reference in designing a microbubble generator. The possibility of the existence of an ultrafine bubble shortly after microbubble generation needs to be studied further, especially its effect on the bubble stability and level of dissolved gas in water.

articleTitle: The Development of Human Machine Interface (HMI) on Antenna Stabilization System
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Engineering and Application (ICSEEA)
abstract: Human Machine Interface (HMI) for antenna stabilization systems has been made. This antenna stabilization system is used for ships but could be also installed on land vehicles with some adjustments. The HMI program has been created based on Graphical User Interface (GUI) using the C programming language with Qt Integrated Development Environment (IDE) on raspberry pi 3. This program was designed to monitor and control the real-time antenna stabilization system. Multithread processing algorithms have been applied to ensure that the program could process the system algorithm, GUI display, motor control, and input/output data at the same time so that no process overlap and system crashed could be avoided. Experiments have been conducted which show that all processes could run in real-time and the antenna stabilization mechanism could work well.

articleTitle: The Influence of NaCl Concentration on Performance of Palm Oil Fuel Heater System
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Engineering and Application (ICSEEA)
abstract: The high utilization and exploitation of fossil fuel have adverse environmental impacts and efforts to overcome these problems are called for. One of the options is to replace fossil fuel with palm oil which has many similar characteristics with diesel fuel. However, palm oil has a higher viscosity level than diesel oil which may cause imperfect atomization in the nozzle. As a result, a heater is needed to alter the viscosity of the palm oil to be comparable to diesel oil. This research aims to analyze the influence of NaCl concentration in the water heater to the performance of the palm oil heater system. The study was conducted experiments on existing water heater on the Palm Oil Fuel Heater System. NaCl is added to the water heater with a concentration of 2%, 4%, 6%, 8%, and 10%, and be compared with a pure water heater as a reference. From the experiment, known that an increase in NaCl concentration will cause an increase in the boiling point of the water heater, a reduction in heating time, an increase in the output temperature of palm oil. By adding 10% NaCl to the water heater, the heating time will be reduced by 13,6%. However, the addition of this concentration will also cause less optimal heat propagation by conduction from the water heater to palm oil.

articleTitle: Experimental Investigation of Phase Change Materials Thermal Barriers in Electric Vehicle Battery Module
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Engineering and Application (ICSEEA)
abstract: The use of Phase Change Materials (PCMs) as thermal barriers inside the Electric Vehicles (EV) battery module is experimentally investigated. Generally a proper Battery Thermal Management System is required to maintain the battery system in its optimum performance. In this study, paraffin is selected as the PCM for the BTMS and is applied in the battery module in form of a thermal wall between some battery cells. The location of the PCM-filled tubes and their subsequent effect is experimentally evaluated as the module is connected to dummy loads under forced convection from a blower. The PCM is also used as an airflow barrier to prevent the upstream battery cells getting too much cooling air while the rests have temperature rise. It is found that a suitable placement of the PCM could notably reduce the temperature non-uniformity that may lead to an increase of the battery module overall performance and durability.

articleTitle: Stress Distribution of Bolted Joint Connection in a Hybrid Composite-Steel Chassis
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Engineering and Application (ICSEEA)
abstract: Stress distribution of bolted joint hybrid composite-steel in a vehicle structure is analyzed in this paper. The analysis was carried out on three different conditions that are when the vehicle in total load, in cornering and braking condition. Finite Element Analysis (FEA) is used to investigate the structural behavior during those three different loading conditions. Different parameters were applied for each simulation. The results show that the maximum stress did not appear in the bolted joint area means the stress on this joint is still below the maximum stress of both composite and steel materials with stress value on this area in full load condition is 62 MPa, 54 MPa in cornering condition and 51 MPa in braking condition. By using this hybrid composite-steel chassis structure a lighter weight is obtained. The simulation shows the chassis weight is reduced by about 22.7% compared to full steel chassis with the same dimension.

articleTitle: A New Transformerless High Voltage Gain DC-DC Converter for DC Microgrid
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Engineering and Application (ICSEEA)
abstract: Due to low voltage generation from the Photovoltaic system in Microgrid, a high voltage gain converter is needed to step up the voltage. One type of converter that has high voltage gain is an isolated converter. An isolated converter that usually comes with a transformer or coupled inductor leads to transformer core saturation problem that will increase the power losses, and the usage of the transformer makes this type of converter has a bigger size and dimension. To fix that, a new dc-dc converter topology is developed in this paper to acquire high voltage gain without using any transformer. This proposed dc-dc converter is using the active switches capacitor technique to achieve high voltage gain. The addition of a new configuration in this new topology leads to low voltage ripple on its capacitors, low voltage stress on its switches, and diodes. The steady-state analysis and comparative analysis are discussed in detail. Then, to verify the analysis result, simulation is done in this paper using the PSIM application.

articleTitle: Speed Synchronization Technique for a Multi DC Motor System Using Serial Synchronization
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Engineering and Application (ICSEEA)
abstract: This paper proposed speed synchronization technique for multi DC motors systems using cross coupling and master slave technique with serial connection. Basically, the synchronization technique is master slave but has two master motors. Speed synchronization multi motor is essential in industrial environment with such as conveyor, automation robotic and rolling mills systems. In steel production synchronization failure can also producing low quality product. DC motor still preferred used for some reason like easy to control, high torque in various speed and excellence performance for large inertia load. In this paper speed synchronization archived by high coupled speed control where every DC motor influence each other. When there is load change at one motor and make speed change will affect to other motor. Simplified PID constant regulation also proposed in this paper. Simulation result in Matlab-Simulink shows good synchronization performance measure by Integral Absolute Error (IAE), with small steady state error is maintained.

articleTitle: Energy Management System for Sustainable Operation of Robot in Disaster Response
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Engineering and Application (ICSEEA)
abstract: The search and rescue (SAR) robot needs a long-endurance energy source to extend the mission. It needs the energy harvesting and management system. One of the options to harvest energy from the environment is to use photovoltaic (PV). However, the energy which is generated by the PV fluctuates. Putting a supercapacitor to the system will solve this shortcoming. Moreover, it also supports the battery to handle abrupt load variations. The proportional-integral and fuzzy logic control (PI-FLC) is adopted to determine the powersharing between the battery and the supercapacitor. The low pass filter (LPF) is added to separate a high and low frequency of the load. The supercapacitor error voltage and the high frequency are employed as the input of FLC and the output of FLC is reference power which will be taken from the supercapacitor. The PI controller will regulate the supercapacitor current approaching reference power that is given by the FLC. The simulation using Simpower toolbox MATLAB is conducted to evaluate comprehensively and it proves that the proposed method can maintain the state of charge (SoC) of supercapacitor in that the desired level i.e 38%.

articleTitle: Gravitational Water Vortex Hydropower: Experimental Investigation of Free Surface Wave in Water Intake Channel
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Engineering and Application (ICSEEA)
abstract: Development program for construction of irrigation channel gives big opportunity for development of renewable energy from small low head hydropower source. The use of hydropower gives no negative impact to environment, especially for greenhouse emission. A gravitational vortex hydropower is the object of this study, with the focus on the water intake channel using rectangular geometry. An experimental study was conducted to find the influencing parameters on the intake section of the gravitational vortex hydropower. A set of parameters were varied to determine which parameters affecting the water surface at the intake channel. By analyzing the results of the experiments, the influence of parameters on the water intake channel of gravitational vortex hydropower was found. A performance curve for differentiation of flow type and identification of surface contour has been made. Based on the results of the experiment, placing a strainer at 5 cm distance gave 60% higher output power since this setting could reduce the wave speed. Recommendation to have further study in non-dimensional parametric should be considered for increasing efficiency of the gravitational vortex hydropower.

articleTitle: Domestic Component Level of Absorption and Variable Costing Method for Interior Permanent Magnet Motor Cost

articleTitle: Stator Teeth Model for Optimum Flat Linear Permanent Magnet Generators
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Engineering and Application (ICSEEA)
abstract: Direct-drive wave energy converter (WEC) with linear permanent magnet generators (LPMG) has been recognized as an efficient system to convert wave energy to electrical energy. However, it suffers from a significant cogging force during its translator movement. Any attempts to reduce the force should also consider the effects on the electrical output as well as the overall dimension. As teeth salient ends affect the magnetic flux flow, its configuration can impact the cogging force but also induced voltage. Hence, this paper presents several design alternatives of teeth salient ends' shape to achieve optimum cogging force and output voltage without changing the overall size. The voltage and cogging force from different models are extracted by using finite element magnetic-based simulation and analytical calculation. The results show that flat, outward-trapezoid, and outward-quarter rounded salient end models bring the optimum induced voltage and cogging force.

articleTitle: A Compatibility Testing of Using Pure DME as a Replacement of LPG for Gas Stoves
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Engineering and Application (ICSEEA)
abstract: This paper presents the compatibility of pure DME application on the existing single burner LPG stoves distributed in the Indonesian market. The performance of the gas stoves when fueled by LPG and pure DME will be compared. The parameters used for the compatibility analysis include heat input, gas consumption, thermal efficiency, and boiling time. The heat input and efficiency of the gas stove were determined according to SNI 8660:2018 with calorific values adjusted for each gas. The result shows that some gas stoves designed for the use of LPG fuel can also operate when using DME fuel. At the same gas input pressure, there is a change in the performance of the gas stove due to the difference in calorific value between the two fuels. Although the efficiency value of the gas stove produced is not significantly different, but the stove using DME fuel takes longer to boil water than when using LPG fuel.

articleTitle: Performance and Emission Diesel Engine Using Diesel-Normal Heptane Volatility Fuel
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Engineering and Application (ICSEEA)
abstract: Conventional diesel engine have a problem with exhaust gas emission where there is a trade of NOx and soot formation inhibits with emission regulation. For this problem, this paper explores the effect of volatility of fuel in on performance and emission in diesel engine. Diesel fuel was blended with N heptane as a volatility fuel into different massbased fraction (0%, 20 %, 40%, 60%, 80%). Thermodynamic Boost AVL simulation software under two engine load condition (10 Nm and 50 Nm) were simulated at 2200 rpm. The model of the engine using Yanmar TF 155 with 102 x 105 bore and stroke with 17,8 compression ratios. The start of combustion was fixed at 5°CA BTDC with 80-degree combustion duration for all test cases. Pressure in the combustion chamber shows a decrease of up to 15 percent for loads between 10 Nm to 50 Nm loads. The addition of volatility of the fuel indicates the atomization of the fuel and the process of mixing the fuel changes during the ignition delay process. Rate of heat release shows a decrease of up to 7 percent for loads between 10 Nm to 50 Nm loads. In the case of the volatility fuel of diesel/normal heptane, the rate of heat release (ROHR) shows that the higher volatility produced lower and faster than a mixture with less volatility. The high-volatility fuel has effect on NOx and soot emissions. At 10 Nm load and 80% Normal Heptane, the NOx concentration decreased 40 %. While running under 50 Nm load and 80% of Normal Heptane, the NOx concentration decreased 14 %. This is a advantaged of replacing the volatility fuel-air mixture causing a reduction in the heating value of air and fuel. Raising the load increases soot concentration.

articleTitle: Cascaded H-Bridge Dual Active Switched-Capacitor Quasi Z-Source Inverter
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Engineering and Application (ICSEEA)
abstract: This paper proposes a new topology in the family of impedance source cells for multilevel applications. The proposed topology integrates DASC-qZSI with CHB Inverter. The proposed topology has several advantages such as high voltage gain, lower switching device inverter voltage stress, lower diode current stress, lower inductor current ripple, and lower output waveform distortion compared to the previous topology. The proposed topology will be compared with the CHB-qZSI and CFL-qSBI topologies. The parameters compared include boost factor, voltage gain, capacitor voltage stress, diode voltage stress, active switch voltage stress, switching device H-bridge inverter voltage stress, inductor current stress, diode current stress, inductor current ripple, and load current THD. PSIM simulation software is used to validate the operating principle and analysis results of the proposed topology. The proposed CHB-DASC-qZSI is recommended for applications requiring high voltage gain with a maximum ideal voltage gain of 16 and better quality of output power such as photovoltaic (PV) power generation systems.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of a Fan Beam Tomography System for The Performance Evaluation of Geothermal Pipe
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Engineering and Application (ICSEEA)
abstract: Tomography technique as one method of visualizing internal conditions has been developed in the medical tools. Over the last view years, this technique is implemented in the industrial application for inspecting tools, such as in the geothermal industry. The design of the tomography system has been continuously improved from generation to generation by considering the reliability of the system in field. Fan beam tomography system is designed to measure various types of pipe, including geothermal pipe. The aim of this research is to design a fan beam tomography measurement system that adapts to mechanical structure condition and neighborhood. Hereafter to visualize the cross-section of a scaling pipe which varies in material density and geometry. The system is designed to represent 128 detectors that form a fan arc, with the gamma emitter positioned in the center system. Scanning was performed using gamma radiation source of Sc-46 with $15 \times$ 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-3</sup> Curie (15 mCi) activity. The system is driven by using two motors assisted by Arduino and Labview software based for automation and data acquisition. Fan projection angle 100 degrees and fan rotation increment of the scan is 5.625 degrees. The results shows that the system design is successful in visualizing cross-section of scaling pipe, as well as distinguish the density and geometry of the material. Scale or foreign materials are identified in geothermal pipe image, and brings harms in reducing performance during operation. Image reconstruction using the MATLAB application with measurement error analysis obtained values below 5%. It can be concluded that the fan beam tomography system prototype design is successful in displaying cross-sectional images and evaluating the performance of geothermal pipes.

articleTitle: Data Smoothing of a Real-life Driving Test Result
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Engineering and Application (ICSEEA)
abstract: A result of a real-life driving test observation usually consists of data that contains high irregularity. As a result, the shape of data trends from observations becomes difficult to know. Therefore, data that contain high irregularity in time series analysis are processed using the data smoothing method. In this study, a dataset of real-life driving tests observation of an electric vehicle is processed using the Simple Moving Average (SMA), Single Exponential Smoothing (SES), and Double Exponential Smoothing (DES) methods. Furthermore, the evaluation of each data smoothing results using Mean Arctangent Absolute Percentage Error (MAAPE). The results of data smoothing show that the lowest MAAPE is 0.252, which is generated through the SES method with data smoothing constant of 0.9. This indicates that SES with data smoothing constant of 0.9 produces data smoothing that is closest to the original data or has the smallest deviation with the original data, but data trends are difficult to know because they still contain high irregularity. Conversely, the data trend is clearly visible by the results of SMA data smoothing with a period constant of 250 with a MAAPE value of 0.793, despite having the greatest deviation with the original data. For the purpose of knowing trends in this study, SMA with a period constant of 250 shows the best results. For related studies, this trend from data smoothing could be used as a standard cycle (driving cycle in certain environments) on components and electric vehicles test.

articleTitle: Performance Improvement of Grid connected PV System Using Neuro-Fuzzy Controller
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Engineering and Application (ICSEEA)
abstract: This paper studies an adaptive neuro-fuzzy (ANFIS) control for a three-phase grid-connected Photovoltaic (PV) system. This study aims to improve the performances of the system, ensure a high quality of the Total Harmonic Distortion and extract the maximum power while ensuring unity power factor. Due to the complexity of the tracker mechanism and non-linear nature of the photovoltaic system, the artificial intelligence-based ANFIS method is used instead of the two PI regulation loop for grid currents. The validation and training data of the utilized neuro-fuzzy controller are obtained by simulation of the entire system with the PI controllers calculated for variation of solar irradiance. The simulation study shows that the neuro-fuzzy controller indicates significantly more enhanced performance than that of the PI controller, reveals that the active and reactive power are tracked quickly and accurately for variation of irradiance, guarantee power factor unity and ensuring lower overshoot and better total harmonic distortion (THD).

articleTitle: Experimental Test on Utilization of Waste Heat from Grilling Stove for Developing Self-Rotating Fan System
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Engineering and Application (ICSEEA)
abstract: The grilling process in conventional grills generally requires a fanning system to maintain the charcoal embers to be stable. At the same time, there is heat energy lost into the environment by conduction through a grill. This study discussed the use of waste heat from a conventional grilling stove to produce energy to drive the self-rotating fan system. The component used was the thermoelectric module type TEG SP1848 which can convert heat energy into electrical energy. The experiment was carried out in two stages. The first step was testing the temperature characteristics produced on both the hot-side and cold-side of thermoelectric using 2 treatments (with water in the heatsink and without water). The second stage was the experiment by using 3 variations of the thermoelectric configuration i.e. single module, a double module using a series circuit, and a double module using a parallel circuit. Observation results had shown that the use of water can stabilize the temperature on the cold side of TEG and the temperature was lower than without water. Besides, there was a positive trend indication between ΔT and voltage as well as ΔT and electric current where increase in ΔT increase in voltage and current so that the power generated was also higher. The power generated during the grilling process had been able to rotate the 3 V DC self-rotating fan system. Experimental results had shown that the use of a dual parallel configuration produced the highest power with an average voltage of 1.80 V, an electric current of 1.8 mA, and an average ΔT of 48.8 °C.

articleTitle: Dynamic Inductance Simulation of a Linear Permanent Magnet Generator Under Different Magnet Configurations
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Engineering and Application (ICSEEA)
abstract: Recently, some innovations have been applied to the linear permanent magnet generator (LPMG). They are including the introduction of high-remanence rare-earth magnets and the use of different magnet configurations. However, these actions also affect the flow and distribution of the magnetic flux. Under the load condition, the load current will also generate reverse flux. The flux resultant then affects the coil parameters; the significant one is the coil inductance. Since it is influential to the output voltage and output power profiles, the impact study of the permanent magnet settings under load condition is essential. Hence this paper presents the inductance profile study of the LMPG with different magnet configurations. After presenting the initial designs, several magnet settings including the material and configuration were varied. Finite element magnetic simulation and analytical calculations were then performed to obtain the inductance profile of the LPMG. The results show that the inductance value varies with change in load current and magnet position. The different magnet materials (SmCo 30 and N35) do not significantly affect the inductance. Meanwhile, different magnet configuration (radial, axial, halbach) results in different inductance trends.

articleTitle: Optimal Placement and Sizing of PV as DG for Losses Minimization Using PSO Algorithm: a Case in Purworejo Area
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Engineering and Application (ICSEEA)
abstract: The Total distribution system losses of PT PLN ULP Purworejo reach 10.467%as technical and non-technical losses which were very high compare to the maximum limit (5%). In this research, Photovoltaics (PV) Distributed Generation (DG) was installed as an active power injection to reduce the system's losses. This research determined the hosting capacity of PV including the location and capacity of the PV. The problem was modeled into an optimization problem and was simulated using Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) algorithm in MATLAB environment. The simulation was considered the voltage, power factor (pf), and branch current as constraints. The simulation was conducted on the existing system of Feeder 7 of PT PLN ULP Purworejo distribution system. Backward Forward Sweep (BFS) method was used for load flow analysis. As the load flow analysis result, the technical losses on a feeder 7 reach 2.676% of feeder 7 supply. The simulation results showed that by installing optimal distributed PV, the technical losses in feeder 7 were reduced to 1.351%. The overall losses of PT PLN ULP Purworejo become 10.045%.

articleTitle: Study of Harmonic Mitigation Techniques Based on Ranges Level Voltage Refer to IEEE 519-2014
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Engineering and Application (ICSEEA)
abstract: The use of semiconductor-based electrical and electronic devices has been known to be widespread and applied in all fields due to increased efficiency and energy saving. But on the other side, the use of non-linear loads, causing power quality problems in the electric power system so that it becomes an important issue and must be overcome, one of which is Harmonic. Harmonics is a disturbance that occurs in an electric power distribution system due to the distortion of current and voltage waves. In this paper discusses the harmonic phenomenon, harmonic standards and harmonic mitigation technology. The discussed harmonic standards refer to IEEE 519-2014 and IEC 6100-3-2. Due to the large number and variety of methods available, the harmonic mitigation techniques are grouped into 3 categories, including passive harmonic filters, active harmonic filters and hybrid harmonic filters. The use of harmonic filters, among others, is adjusted to the voltage level and conditions of the electric power system. From the study results it is known that to suppress harmonic distortion for levels voltage of V ≤ 1.0 kV using passive harmonic filters and DC chokes, at a distribution level voltage of 1.0 kV <; V ≤ 69 kV using a zigzag transformer mounted on the load side of the distribution transformer, at level voltage of 69 kV ≤ 161 kV using a hybrid filter technique. Meanwhile, to reduce harmonics at a level voltage of V> 161 kV by keeping the voltage level of the transformer operating at its nominal voltage.

articleTitle: The Study of Shared-Autonomous Vehicle Design Concept for Urban Public Transportation in Indonesia
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Engineering and Application (ICSEEA)
abstract: An integrated public transport system in the urban areas has been a great challenge in Indonesia, especially regarding connectivity between the mass transport modes with the first mile/last mile (FMLM) transport. This study discusses the application of universal design (UD) for future urban public transport in Indonesia which will be based on electrically powered autonomous vehicles (AV). The universal design concept of AV coupled with the sharing economy concept will allow the realization of a transport system that is both eco-friendly and user-friendly. The sharing economy will optimize the consumption pattern by preventing the occurrence of excessive usage of resources and underutilized assets. The concept of UD involves seven principles approach which covers equitable use, flexibility in use, simple and intuitive use, perceptible information, tolerance for error, low physical effort, size and space for approach and use. The design concept illustrates the application of UD and sharing economy through the design of smartphone platform applications, AV fleets, supporting infrastructure tailored for AV operation, and ideation. The applicability of UD and sharing economy in the future urban AV will increase the possibility of its adoption in the public transport system. The concept will define the features necessary for an ideal scenario of the ideation process. Furthermore, accessibility is the key to the UD approach, as the principle will allow not only people with special needs but a wide range of users to use it more easily. The application of this concept, in the end, will induce urban population to use public transport instead of private vehicles that create traffic congestion.

articleTitle: Piezoelectric Array Configuration Technique into Enhance Power Catchment for Sound Energy Harvester System
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Engineering and Application (ICSEEA)
abstract: The objective of this study is to explore the harvest maximum output changes occurs in piezoelectric transducer when connected in different configuration to produce highest electricity consumption and generate sound energy harvesting system. Acoustic energy is a type of environmental energy source that can be extracted and converted into electrical energy for small-scale energy applications. In this study, the corresponding load resistance for single piezoelectric transducer is 4.5 kΩ, together with a constant vibration source at a frequency of 68 Hz and a 1-g acceleration. The performance of output voltage and power of piezoelectric are evaluated and the optimum output is measured by depending on the connection of the piezoelectric transducer arrangement into series, parallel and series, and parallel which stimulated using Proteus software. The experiment result presented that, when have single piezo, 5 piezo connected in series, and 5 piezo connected in parallel, the output powers are 1.664 mW, 1.671mW and 7.676 mW, respectively. During the combination series and parallel connections, the output power of 3S1P piezo increases to 5.05mW. In a parallel configuration, the output voltage that produced is much higher than a piezoelectric transducer arrangement connected in series connection. The piezoelectric transducer that connected in parallel configurations increases its voltage output from 2.83 V to 13.05 V with the same polarity. The arrangement of piezoelectric transducer in parallel configuration is affordable, with its higher production of a higher power output compared to the arrangement of piezoelectric transducer in series connection. Whereas in terms of power output, the maximum power remains constant in the range of 1.665 to 1.671 mW when three transducers are in series configuration connection with the same polarity. In conclusion, the proper implementation of the piezoelectric array configuration is needed in order to operate the minimum energy for low load devices and promise to accomplish generated optimum power output in harvester system.

articleTitle: Utilization of Water Energy Potential on Tail Race for Very Low Head Hydro Power Plant
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Engineering and Application (ICSEEA)
abstract: In a hydro power plant (HPP), water that passes through a turbine will flow into the tailrace and flow back into the water channel. Water energy can be used to generate electrical power using a very low head-type turbine. However, currently, energy from HPP tail water has not been appropriately utilized. This paper discusses the study of various types of very low head hydro power to exploit the potential of electrical energy in the HPP disposal channel. The chosen location is the Dago HPP, located in Bandung, West Java, owned by PT. Indonesia Power. Technical studies are necessary to determine the magnitude of electrical energy's potential, the suitable type of technology application, and the investment costs requirement. The location survey knew that the Dago HPP has an average flow rate of 1.192 m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>/s, 1.7 m of the head, and the potential electrical energy generation is around 13.9 kW. Several types of very low power plants apply as alternatives: water wheels, Archimedes screw turbines, propeller submersible turbines, and vortex turbines. Building Micro Hydro Power Plant (MHPP) using a waterwheel required an investment cost of around IDR 335 million, an Archimedes screw turbine of IDR 445 million, a submersible propeller turbine of IDR 360 million, and a vortex turbine of IDR 315 million. The comparison from the four VLH shows that the Vortex turbine is the most potential technology because it produces a large amount of electrical energy at the cheapest investment cost.

articleTitle: A Parametric of Basin Geometry of Gravitational Water Vortex Power Plant
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Engineering and Application (ICSEEA)
abstract: Energy demand is increasing and it raise a climate change issue. Greenhouse emissions, depleted fossil energy resources, increasing fossil energy cost are reasons to maximize the utilization of renewable energy source. Hydropower extend an alternative energy source to cover the growing energy demand and release no emission at the same time for maintaining the climate change. In recent years, major focus of hydropower research is moving to small hydropower, as large hydropower opportunities are exploited and have high capital expenditure to build. A water vortex stream is a common phenomenon that we can see everyday life. Water flow out from the bathtub through outlet or water flow down in the sink after we finish washing the dishes, that is what we call vortex flow. and is a free-surface flow, homogenous fluid that contained water and air. This water vortex can be applied in low head small hydropower plant, recently known as gravitational water vortex power plant. River off Gravitational Water Vortex power plant (GWVPP) is one of low head turbine that can be used to generate electricity in small scale, pico-hydro. This study is focus on basin geometry. Models are developed to investigate the outlet diameter, depth discharge and basin geometry. It is found out that parameter of the basin should refer to source, which are flow rate, and the head of the water. It shows that spiral geometry for the basin gives symmetric and strong vortex and can be used as an alternative of conical basin.

articleTitle: Conceptual Design of Universal Autonomous Platform for Micromobility and Delivery System in the Hospital
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Engineering and Application (ICSEEA)
abstract: Micro mobility is described as either human-powered or electrically-powered vehicle with maximum speed of 25 km/h and weight of less than 500 kg. The hospital trolleys for delivery of medical supplies are one example of micro mobility. This study introduces the conceptual design of a universal autonomous platform as a replacement for the hospital trolleys to solve the problem of musculoskeletal complaints among the trolley operators. The introduction of the Industry 4.0 concept involving the internet of things (IoT) and the cyber-physical system has made the idea possible to realize. In the first stage, we performed problems seeking ergonomic and design issues on the current trolleys by observation and interview. As expected, manual materials handling (MMH) to operate the trolley manually induces musculoskeletal complaints especially low back pain. The ergonomic problems then analyzed and taken into design consideration thoroughly during the design process. In the design concept, we will eliminate MMH as much as possible by the introduction of an autonomous micro vehicle as a modular platform. The modular platform will be able to accommodate various types of the superstructure to perform the various functions which the current hospital trolleys are serving.

articleTitle: A Review: Gravitational Water Vortex Power Plant
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Engineering and Application (ICSEEA)
abstract: Significant population and economic growth, caused increasing of energy demand. Depletion of fossil fuel moreover coupled by climate change issue that caused by increasing carbon emission, become necessity to continuously encourage achieving renewable energy mix in energy primer. Large potentials of hydro renewable energy source and small utilization of it, micro-hydro and pico-hydro power plant are suitable to develop especially in country side. The research gap in the current turbine application chart is a challenge for Gravitational Water Vortex Power Plant (GWVPP) strong existence in pico-hydro power, besides conventional turbine design has been developed into it. However, development in vortex flow and basin geometry design has a robust design for the past 10 years of research. Researches have been conducted in few countries that proofed GWVPP has less capital investment and low operational and maintenance cost, however the parameter of the GWVPP still need further development since the power output efficiency still low. Since basin opening and outlet diameter are the main parameters to define basin geometry, inlet channel need to do further research. The research will improve the recent gaps; therefore, vortex turbine could be developed accordingly that would result immediate improvements for renewable energy growth in Indonesia through GWVPP.

articleTitle: Watershed Management for Micro Hydropower Plant Sustainability: Malabar, Indonesia
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Engineering and Application (ICSEEA)
abstract: The purpose of this research is to analyze the watershed management system for the sustainability of hydropower plants. The two main parameters needed to produce electrical energy are water flow and head. Water flow depends on the watershed area, rainfall, and land cover, which affects the runoff and infiltration volume. Good land cover has a large infiltration volume so that it can infiltrate rainwater into the ground and become the reserved water to maintain base flow during the dry season. Malabar Micro Hydropower Plant (MHP), Bandung, West Java, Indonesia, was selected as the case study. There are no significant land-use changes in this area resulting in a stable base flow, which allows MHP to work well until now. The base flow can be continuously maintained at a value not less than 3 $m^{3}/s$, the same as the designed discharge of the power plant. The land-use changes are possible as long as the flow is not lower than the minimum base flow. It can be employed by using a high infiltration coefficient of land cover and artificial recharge groundwater techniques..

articleTitle: Analysis of Energy Policy in Indonesia (Intermestic Model Approach)
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Engineering and Application (ICSEEA)
abstract: The energy sector is important not only as a foreign exchange earner but also in the real sector, because it supports the fuel needs of the community. Therefore, the role of policies to support the energy sector to continue to grow and develop is very necessary and starting from old older until the reform older that energy policy have changed. This change is according to socio political conditions and community needs such as the Mining Law, Oil and Gas Law and the Electricity Law. Policies in the energy sector carried out gradually, they cannot be changed drastically. These changes are based on the constitution made following market developments, geopolitical turmoil and demands for globalization so that policy transformation in the energy sector continues. This study uses a qualitative approach. Data collection techniques are carried out by reviewing statutory regulations and observations. The results of the study show that the role of ideas and interests of domestic and international actors are equally important in the process of transformation energy sector policies using the intermestic model.
